questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Adsorption of a gas on an adsorbent follows Freundlich adsorption isotherm. The slope and intercept (on $y$-axis) of the isotherm are 0.5 and 1.0 respectively. What is the value of $\frac{x}{m}$, when the pressure of the gas $(\mathrm{A})$ is 100 atm ?
questions.solution:
$Freundlich isotherm.
\begin{aligned} & \ln \frac{x}{m}=\ln k+\frac{1}{n} \ln p \\ & \text{ or, } \log \frac{x}{m}=\log k+\frac{1}{n} \log p \\ & y=c+m x \\ & \text{ Slope }(m)=\frac{1}{n} \quad \therefore \quad \frac{1}{n}=0.5 \\ & \text{ Intercept }(\mathrm{c})=\log k=1 \\ & \text{ Pressure }(p)=100 \text{ atm } \\ & \therefore \log \frac{x}{m}=1+0.5 \log 10^2 \\ & \log \frac{x}{m}=1+0.5 \times 2 \Rightarrow \log \frac{x}{m}=2 \\ & \frac{x}{m}=10^2=100\end{aligned}$

questions.q: For precipitating $\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ sol, the best precipitating agent is
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ is a positive sol, hence the best coagulant for precipitation of $\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ is $\mathrm{Na}_3 \left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right].$ The $precipitating effect of an ion on dispersed phase of opposite charge increases with the valence of ions. According to Hardy-Schulze rule, greater is the valency of ions, greater is its power to bring about coagulation.
\begin{aligned} \mathrm{Na}_3 \left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]& \longrightarrow 3 \mathrm{Na}^{+}+\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-}\\ \mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{SO}_{4} & \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{Na}^{+}+\mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-} \\ \mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{OH})_3& \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cr}^{3+}+3 \mathrm{OH}^{-}\\ \mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{OH})_3& \longrightarrow \mathrm{Al}^{3+}+3 \mathrm{OH}^{-} \end{aligned}The ion with highest negative valency will coagulate positive sol of \mathrm{Fe}$($\mathrm{OH}$)_3$ is \left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-}$. As it has highest coagulating power from relation (i), it would have lowest flocculating value and hence, is the best agent for coagulation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statements is/are not correct?
(A) Adsorption is accompanied by decrease in enthalpy as well as decrease in entropy of the system.
(B) Gases, which can react strongly with adsorbent show chemisorption.
(C) When the value of the slope of the Freundlich isotherm is non-zero, adsorption is independent of pressure.
(D) Gold number of potato starch is 0.15.
questions.solution:
(A) Adsorption is accompained by decrease in enthalpy as well as in entropy of the system $\Delta G=\Delta H-T \Delta S$ and adsorption is an exothermic process [ thus has $\Delta H=(-)$ ve, i.e. decreases] and randomness, i.e. ( $\Delta$ S) also decreases because after adsorption free movement is restricted, but to make the $\Delta G(-)$ ve, $\Delta H > T$. $\Delta S$. Hence, the statement (A) is correct.
(B) Gases, which can react strongly with adsorbent show chemisorption as they form chemical bonds with the adsorbent. Hence, the statement (c) is also correct.
(C) When the value of slope of the Freundlich isotherm is non-zero, adsorption of a gas depends on pressure over it, till the adsorption is possible. According to Freundlich isotherm equation :
$\frac{x}{m}=k \cdot p^{1 / n}$
where,
$x=$ mass of gas adsorbed,
$m=$ mass of adsorbent,
$p=$ pressure,
$k=$ constant,
$n=$ integer number,
Hence, statement (C) is not correct.
(D) Gold number is defined as, "The number of milligrams of a hydropbilic colloid that will just prevent the precipitation of $10 \mathrm{ mL}$ of a pold sol on the addition of $1 \mathrm{ mL}$ of $10 \%$ sodium chloride solution". Gold number for patalo starch is 20
Hence, statements (C) and (D) are not correct and therefore (d) is the correct option.

Effect of temperature :Mostly the process of adsorption is exothermic and the reverse process or desorption is endothermic. Physical adsorption decreases continuously with increase in temperature whereas chemisorption increases initially, shows a maximum in the curve, and then it decreases continuously.

Hence, the plot a and c represent the& chemisorption.

questions.q: Which of the following is true for spontaneous adsorption?
questions.solution:
Adsorption processes are exothermic $(\Delta H < 0)$ and degree of randomness of adsorbate particles decreases, i.e. $\Delta S < 0$.
According to Gibbs' equation, $\Delta G=\Delta H-T \Delta S$ at lower temperature adsorption becomes spontaneous, i.e. $\Delta G < 0$

questions.solution: Freundlich adsorption isotherm is as $\frac{x}{m}=K p^{1 / n}$ Taking logarithms on both sides $\log \frac{x}{m}=\log K+\frac{1}{n} \log p$ On plotting a graph between $\log x / m$ and $\log p$, a straight line will be obtained.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A micelle formed during the cleansing action by soap is
options: aggregated particles of soap and dirt
an aggregated particle of dust and water
questions.solution: Soap contains hydrophobic (ie, fat soluble or water repelling) as well as hydrophilic (water soluble) end. Hydrophobic end remains soluble in dust or grease particles while hydrophilic end is attracted towards water. Hence, several hydrophobic pocket surrounds the grease particles. This aggregate of soap and dirt is called micelle. On washing with plenty of water dust is removed along with soap.

Both $(A)$ and $(R)$ are true but $(R)$ is not the correct explanation of $(\mathrm{A})$
(A) is true, but (R) is not true
(A) is not true, but (R) is true
questions.solution: A catalyst increases the rate of reaction because in the presence of catalyst the activation energy of the reaction decreases.
